messages:
li (support): heads up — customer (acme-analytics) reports sustained 502/504s to hosted inference in us-west-2.az2 since ~14:50 PST. They see request timeouts and auth retries. forwarding logs and curl repro below. can we triage?

mike (oncall-bot): ALERT: hosted-api.5xx.rate spike in us-west-2.az2 (14:49—14:56). CPU unchanged, network error rate up. https://grafana.redwood.example/d/Alerts/hosted-api-5xx (automated) :warning:

liam (customer): posting sample: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'` -> `502 Bad Gateway` intermittently, ~30% of requests during window.

li (support): attaching GC/edge logs from their session:
```
[2026-03-17T14:50:12Z] upstream read timeout: tls handshake failed: i/o timeout
[2026-03-17T14:50:13Z] retrying request, attempt=2
[2026-03-17T14:50:13Z] auth refresh error: control-plane timeout
[2026-03-17T14:50:14Z] response 502 gateway from edge-az2-eu
```

omar (netops): I see ECMP path-flapping to our SFO transit peer servicing az2. Packet reorder+microbursts ~1-3% for short bursts (10–30s) starting 14:49. BGP AS path changed to prefer provider-X then flapped back. Provider-side logs show link transients on peer-3.

alex (eng-runtime): runtime metrics line up — KV cache miss ratio spikes and tail latency jumps during those microbursts. When upstream TLS fails we observe fallback to model-variant route, but retries are tight and contribute to 502s. snippet from runtime logs: 
```
[runtime] request_id=abc123 seq=45 status=upstream_error backend=edge-az2 err="tls: handshake timeout"
[router] fallback -> variant-small (latency tradeoff)
```

jen (sre): can we fail traffic off az2 to az1 for hosted API customers in that AZ? what's the policy for cross-az failover for hosted?

omar (netops): short term: yes — we can adjust BGP local-pref to prefer upstream-B for az2 egress and advertise less specific to provider-X. doing it now as a manual mitigation. will monitor STA counters.

k8s-deploy-bot: route-preference-change applied to us-west-2.az2 (manual by omar).

li (support): customer updated: they still see occasional 502s but much reduced. they've also reported some 401s during the spike — could be token refreshes failing while control-plane calls timeout.

alex (eng-runtime): 401s are probable collateral when the auth service RPCs hit timeouts. I'll push a short-term change to increase auth RPC timeout and add jittered backoff for token refresh in the SDK (non-blocking fallback to cached token). will deploy to hosted control-plane in the next 10m.

jen (sre): also throttles for retry storm? we should ensure we don't amplify load with aggressive retries from edge. Can we add per-route retry budget?

alex (eng-runtime): adding a soft retry budget on edge proxies now (max 2 retries, exponential backoff, jitter). patch will roll in 5m.

omar (netops): provider acknowledged a short physical flap on peer-3; they're running fiber tests and will escalate with on-call at provider.

li (support): logging ticket INC-20260317-ACME and sending customer post-mortem link once we have it. example repro steps captured: 
1) curl twice fast -> one succeeds, one 502
2) replay at low qps -> stable
3) sustained burst qps 50+ -> more likely to trigger 5xx during microbursts

liam (customer): thanks team, appreciate the quick response. will keep monitoring from our side.

mike (oncall-bot): POST-MITIGATION CHECK (15:05 PST): 5xx rate down to baseline in us-west-2.az2, packet reorder noise still under provider review. Marking incident as mitigated — will keep in watch for 2h. :white_check_mark:
